The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.

Regarding the thematic structure in the provided text, the author’s motive appears to be the exploration of the parallel between botanical decay and human emotional isolation. By using the sunflower’s wilting as a mirror for the protagonist’s sadness, the author structurally links the natural cycle of life and decay with the fragility of human connection. This metaphor serves to urge readers to reflect on how neglect—whether directed at a plant or a relationship—leads to inevitable deterioration, thereby reinforcing the theme that care and attention are essential for sustaining both nature and personal bonds.
